sections.title: Introduction to Ken Doll Design
sections.content: The Ken Doll design process involves multiple components and considerations to ensure quality and consistency across products. This guideline provides an overview of the dual sourcing strategy and the use of 3D models in the design process.

sections.title: Dual Sourcing Strategy
sections.content: The Ken Doll utilizes a dual sourcing strategy involving PTMI and MCA. This approach ensures that production can continue smoothly even if one source encounters issues. Dual sourcing is critical for maintaining supply chain resilience and product availability.

sections.title: 3D Model Utilization
sections.content: 3D models are integral to the Ken Doll design process. They allow for precise visualization and modification of the doll's features before physical prototypes are created. This reduces errors and speeds up the development cycle.

sections.title: Component Identification
sections.content: Each Ken Doll component is identified with specific codes, such as DWK47 and FNH40. These codes help in tracking and managing parts throughout the production process, ensuring that each component meets the required standards.

sections.title: Introduction to Chelsea Doll Variants
sections.content: The Chelsea Doll series includes several variants, each identified by unique codes such as CH-4(V3283), CH-7(V7005), and CH-6(V0573). These variants are dual-sourced from PTMI & MCA and utilize CDI for their design and manufacturing processes. Each variant is accompanied by a 3D model to aid in visualization and design refinement.

sections.title: Chelsea Doll Assembly and Production
sections.content: The assembly of Chelsea dolls involves a combination of torsos, arms, and legs. For example, the 'Chelsea with Bodice-A' configuration includes 9 torsos, 6 arms, and 1 leg, resulting in a total of 54 dolls. In contrast, the 'Chelsea with Bodice-B' configuration includes 15 torsos, 6 arms, and 1 leg, resulting in a total of 90 dolls. This modular approach allows for efficient production scaling and customization.

sections.title: Introduction to Collector Dolls
sections.content: Collector dolls are categorized into various models such as Model Muse, Holiday Doll, Pivotal Doll, Silkstone Barbie, and Uhura. Each model has unique identifiers and may be sourced from different manufacturers, indicated by codes such as B3457-dual source and W3420-PTMI.

sections.title: Model Identification and Resources
sections.content: Each collector doll model is associated with specific codes that help in identifying the source and type of the doll. For instance, the Model Muse is identified by B3457-dual source, while the Holiday Doll is identified by W3420-PTMI. These codes are crucial for cataloging and sourcing purposes. Additionally, resources such as photos and 3D models are available for each doll model to aid in design and manufacturing processes.

sections.title: Design and Manufacturing Considerations
sections.content: When designing collector dolls, it is important to consider the availability of resources such as photos and 3D models. These resources provide detailed visual and structural information that is essential for accurate reproduction and quality control. For example, the Vintage Doll and Wonder Woman models have associated photos and 3D models that can be used to ensure design fidelity.

sections.title: Special Models and Variants
sections.content: Special models such as the Vintage Skipper, Vintage Barbie, and themed dolls like Batman and Wonder Woman have unique identifiers and resources. These models often require special attention to detail and adherence to specific design guidelines to maintain their collectible value. For instance, the Vintage Barbie is identified by DGW46-PTMI and has associated photos and 3D models for reference.

sections.title: Neck Connector Design
sections.content: The neck connector design should ensure a secure fit while allowing for smooth movement. Considerations for material selection and connector geometry are crucial to prevent wear and tear over time.

sections.title: Arm Design
sections.content: Arm design must accommodate the insert molding process. Ensure that the connector's outer diameter is between 0.3-0.5mm to facilitate easy assembly and disassembly. This is crucial for both upper and lower arm components.

sections.title: Barbie Insert Arm Guideline
sections.content: For the Barbie arm and shoulder connector, the design should minimize insert mold issues. Ensure the connector fits snugly into the torso while allowing for rotational movement. The design should also consider the shut-off hole dimensions to maintain structural integrity.

sections.title: Torso Design
sections.content: The torso design should integrate seamlessly with the neck and arm connectors. It must support the overall structure of the doll while allowing for flexibility and durability. Consider the use of lightweight materials to enhance playability.

sections.title: Leg Plug-In Design
sections.content: The leg plug-in design should ensure stability and ease of assembly. The connector should be designed to prevent accidental detachment while allowing for smooth movement. The outer diameter at the connection point should be between 0.3-0.5mm.

sections.title: Bonding and Welding Techniques
sections.content: PTMI utilizes solvent bonding for assembly, whereas MCA employs sonic welding. Each method has its own advantages and should be chosen based on the specific requirements of the toy design.

sections.title: Arm Design Considerations
sections.content: To prevent scratching issues on the arm ball, ensure there is sufficient clearance and that the center alignment is correct. Refer to the detailed arm design specifications for precise measurements and tolerances.

sections.title: Shoulder Gap Minimization
sections.content: Ensure there are no visible gaps at the shoulder joints. This is crucial for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity.

sections.title: Torso Design Updates
sections.content: For new toy developments, use the updated torso Pro-E model. This ensures compatibility with the latest design standards and improvements. Refer to the torso design documentation for detailed guidelines.

sections.title: Neck Connector Design Overview
sections.content: The Barbie neck connector design has evolved over time, with a transition from a long neck connector to a short version, which was phased out based on design direction. This change was implemented to improve the overall aesthetics and functionality of the Barbie doll.

sections.title: Neck Connector Pin Specifications
sections.content: Since June 2014, the neck connector pin at the torso rear for PTMI and MCA models has been standardized to the PTMI version. This design requires a radius at the pin root area and a recess on the opposite side to secure the pin effectively. These modifications ensure a more robust connection and enhance the doll's durability during play.

sections.title: Key Dimensions
sections.content: The key dimensions for the neck connector design are crucial for ensuring compatibility and functionality across different Barbie models. While specific measurements are not provided in the raw data, it is essential to adhere to the standardized dimensions used in the PTMI version for consistency.

sections.title: Arm Ball and Socket Design
sections.content: Ensure the arm's ball and socket design minimizes the risk of scratching. This can be achieved by smoothing the edges and ensuring a snug fit between the ball and socket components.

sections.title: Material and Wall Thickness Considerations
sections.content: The key dimensions, MCA (Material Cross-sectional Area), and PTMI (Part Thickness Minimum Indicator) should be carefully considered as they differ in wall thickness. This requires precise measurement and material selection to ensure durability and functionality.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for the design of insert molding tools specifically for Barbie doll arms, hands, and legs. The focus is on ensuring precision and quality in the molding process to maintain the aesthetic and functional integrity of the doll parts.

sections.title: Arm Insert Molding Guidelines
sections.content:
- Ensure the mold design accommodates the specific dimensions and contours of the Barbie arm.
- Consider the material flow and cooling channels to prevent defects such as warping or incomplete fills.
- Design the mold to allow for easy ejection of the molded arm without damaging the surface finish.

sections.title: Lower Arm Insert Molding Guidelines
sections.content:
- Pay special attention to the joint areas to ensure smooth articulation.
- Use precision shut-off surfaces to prevent flash and ensure a clean parting line.
- Incorporate venting to avoid air traps that could lead to surface blemishes.

sections.title: Hand Insert Molding Guidelines
sections.content:
- Design the mold with detailed attention to the fingers and thumb to ensure accurate reproduction of the hand's features.
- Implement finger shut-off landing requirements to maintain the integrity of the finger details and prevent flash.
- Ensure the mold allows for consistent material flow to avoid defects in the hand structure.

sections.title: Lower Leg Insert Molding Guidelines
sections.content:
- Focus on the ankle and foot areas to ensure proper fit and articulation with the rest of the doll.
- Design the mold to support the structural integrity of the leg while maintaining flexibility for movement.
- Ensure proper alignment of mold halves to prevent misalignment and part defects.

sections.title: Objective
sections.content: The primary goal is to reduce flash in insert molding processes.

sections.title: Flash Reduction Techniques
sections.content:
1. For insert molded hands and feet, flash often occurs at the connection bones, requiring frequent maintenance. To mitigate this, create recessed lines on both sides of the connection bone to act as a seal.

2. Connection bones are typically made from Nylon or POM. Injection molding parameters significantly affect the overall dimensions of connection bones with runner frames. Critical dimensions must be controlled to ensure quality.

3. Avoid placing ejector pins at the edges of inserts. Ejector pin marks on the connection bone, whether protruding or recessed, can easily lead to flash during molding.

4. Ensure connection bones have a larger draft angle. This facilitates easier placement on the mold, reduces mold damage and wear, and minimizes flash occurrence. Additionally, ensure the mushroom head has sufficient engagement and is rounded to prevent breakage. When the parting line (PL) of the bone aligns with the PL of the hands or feet, increase the draft angle on the bone's rounded side to 3°-5°.

sections.title: Material and Injection Considerations
sections.content:
- For PP or PP+EVA hands, consider the water entry position:
  - Non-gas-assist arm
  - Gas-assist arm
- For PVC hands, determine the appropriate water entry position to ensure optimal molding results.

sections.title: Objective
sections.content: The primary goal is to reduce the occurrence of flash in insert molds for lower arms.

sections.title: Design Considerations for Connection Ribs
sections.content: When designing connection ribs, ensure that the outer diameter of the rib is 0.3mm larger than the insert to prevent flash formation at the joint.

sections.title: Connection Rib and Runner Design
sections.content: The connection rib should be integrated with the runner using a thicker gate to maintain structural integrity and prevent deformation. This design facilitates easy placement of the rib onto the mold and prevents damage during clamping.

sections.title: Material and Dimensional Control
sections.content: Connection ribs are typically made from Nylon or POM. Injection molding parameters significantly affect the overall dimensions of ribs with runner frames. It is crucial to control the critical dimensions provided to ensure quality and consistency.

sections.title: Objective
sections.content: The primary goal is to reduce the flash on hand insert molds.

sections.title: Design Rule for Connection Bones
sections.content: For the palm of the insert mold, when designing the connection bones, ensure that the outer diameter of the connection bone is 0.3mm larger than the palm.

sections.title: Connection Bones and Runners
sections.content: The connection bones should be fixed to the runner using a thicker water inlet. This design ensures that the connection bones and the runner can be considered as a single unit, reducing deformation. The aim is to facilitate easy placement of the connection bones onto the mold and prevent damage to the mold during clamping.

sections.title: Material and Injection Parameters
sections.content: Connection bones are often made of Nylon. The injection molding parameters significantly affect the overall dimensions of connection bones with a RunnerFrame. It is crucial to provide the following critical dimensions for control.

sections.title: Objective
sections.content: The primary goal is to reduce the occurrence of flash on the lower leg of insert molds.

sections.title: Design Considerations for Connection Ribs
sections.content: For the lower leg of insert molds, flash tends to occur at the connection ribs. When designing these ribs, incorporate recessed lines on both sides to act as a sealant.

sections.title: Water Inlet and Runner Design
sections.content: Ensure that the connection ribs and runners are linked with a thicker water inlet. This design choice helps to treat them as a single unit, reducing deformation and facilitating easier placement onto the mold, thus preventing mold damage.

sections.title: Material and Injection Parameters
sections.content: Connection ribs are often made from Nylon. Injection molding parameters significantly affect the overall dimensions of connection ribs with a Runner Frame. It is crucial to provide and control the Critical Dimensions to maintain quality.

sections.title: Goal
sections.content: Reduce flash on the hand.

sections.title: Product Design
sections.content: Keep the fingers as close together as possible and, where possible, on the same parting-line plane. If the height difference between the fingers is too large and there is insufficient shutoff area, flash can readily occur and frequent repairs may be required.

sections.title: Finger Shutoff Area
sections.content: The source identifies a guideline for the finger shutoff area but provides no further design criteria.

sections.title: Tooling Design
sections.content: Add a support post near the palm.

sections.title: Updated Design Usage
sections.content: Ensure that the updated design is used for any new development or when building duplicated molds. This ensures consistency and adherence to the latest standards.

sections.title: Leg Design Options
sections.content: Barbie Dolls feature several leg design options: bendable PVC legs, poseable upper and lower legs, and a lower-cost option with two halves made of ABS plastic.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Barbie leg plug-in design focuses on ensuring secure attachment and easy assembly of the doll's legs. This guideline outlines the key design considerations and specifications for creating a robust plug-in mechanism.

sections.title: Design Specifications
sections.content:
1. **Material Selection**: Use durable, non-toxic plastics that can withstand repeated assembly and disassembly.
2. **Plug-in Mechanism**: Design the plug-in mechanism to allow for a snug fit, preventing accidental detachment while allowing for easy manual removal.
3. **Tolerance Levels**: Maintain tight tolerance levels to ensure consistency across production batches.
4. **Safety Standards**: Ensure all materials and designs comply with international toy safety standards, such as ASTM F963 and EN71.

sections.title: Assembly Process
sections.content:
- **Ease of Assembly**: The design should facilitate quick and intuitive assembly by end-users, typically children.
- **Tool-Free Design**: Ensure that no additional tools are required for assembly or disassembly of the leg components.
- **Visual Indicators**: Incorporate visual indicators or guides to assist in the correct alignment and insertion of the leg plug.

sections.title: Testing and Quality Assurance
sections.content:
- **Durability Testing**: Conduct rigorous testing to simulate wear and tear over time, ensuring the plug-in mechanism remains functional.
- **User Testing**: Perform user testing with a diverse group of children to ensure the design meets usability and safety expectations.
- **Quality Checks**: Implement regular quality checks during production to maintain high standards of product integrity.

sections.title: Dimensional Specifications
sections.content: Ensure the dimensions of the doll parts adhere to the specified measurements. For example, the reference length should be 29.41 mm, and the minimum width should be 3.00 mm.

sections.title: Joint and Connection Design
sections.content: The joints should have a diameter of 1.90 mm with a tolerance of +/- 0.05 mm. Ensure the connection points are designed for easy assembly and disassembly.

sections.title: Base and Stability
sections.content: The base of the doll should be designed to ensure stability. The heart-shaped recess should have a depth of 2.50 mm and a diameter of 1.87 mm with a tolerance of -0.02 mm.

sections.title: Aesthetic and Functional Design
sections.content: The design should balance aesthetics with functionality, ensuring the doll is visually appealing while maintaining structural integrity.

sections.title: Mushroom Fastener Size
sections.content: The recommended size for the mushroom fastener includes a 3.4mm diameter with a 0.4mm radius. The height should be 1.3mm with a 0.8mm 45° chamfer. The hole diameter is 3.0mm with a 1.5mm width and 1.6mm minimum depth. Additional height details should be added if necessary.

sections.title: Belt Assembly Direction
sections.content: For easy assembly, the belt should be tight with the mushroom fastener outward. A loose belt should have the mushroom fastener inward for aesthetic purposes.

sections.title: Pin Location and Direction
sections.content: Pins should be revised to point outward to facilitate dressing on the torso. The current design with pins inward is difficult to dress.

sections.title: Post Alignment
sections.content: Using two posts makes alignment difficult when dressing. It is suggested to use one post for easier alignment.

sections.title: Soft Material Belt Lock Design
sections.content: The design should ensure that the belt lock is secure and easy to use. The GRG29-SS01 design is preferred over the CBN45-QS05 design due to better locking mechanism and ease of use.

sections.title: Recommended Molding Technique
sections.content: The recommended technique involves ensuring the slide moves parallel to the cavity side. This alignment minimizes the risk of flash during the molding process.

sections.title: Not Recommended Molding Technique
sections.content: Avoid having the slide move against the moving cavity side, as this can easily cause flash, leading to defects in the final product.

sections.title: Trimming and Openings in Production
sections.content: Ensure there is an opening on the final product to accommodate the floating core. This may require additional trimming during production to achieve the desired finish.

sections.title: Brush Design Specifications
sections.content: This document provides the standard design specifications for brushes. The image illustrates the critical dimensions and guidelines to ensure optimal performance and manufacturing efficiency.

sections.title: Dimensional Guidelines
sections.content:
- The grid spacing is specified as 0.260 inches.
- Minimum diameter for certain features is 0.060 inches.
- Full radius (R) is required at specified locations to ensure structural integrity.

sections.title: Manufacturing Considerations
sections.content:
- Prioritize maximum material at the root to enhance strength.
- Avoid shrinkage during the manufacturing process to maintain dimensional accuracy.
- A maximum radius of 0.090 inches is allowed at the root for optimal performance.

sections.title: Sharp Edge Requirement
sections.content: Ensure a sharp edge inside along the slide parting line for proper fit and finish.

sections.title: Sharp Point Avoidance
sections.content: Avoid sharp point issues by maintaining a radius greater than 0.8mm.

sections.title: Shut Off Holes Specification
sections.content: Shut off holes should be larger than a diameter of 2mm to ensure proper functionality.

sections.title: Connection Strength
sections.content: Connections should be strong enough, with a minimum thickness greater than 1.2mm, to ensure durability.

sections.title: Production Considerations
sections.content: Ensure openings on the final product for part holding on the floating core. Additional trimming may be required in production.

sections.title: Design Considerations for Earrings
sections.content: When designing earrings, consider the following aspects to ensure comfort, style, and functionality. Earrings should be lightweight to prevent discomfort during extended wear. The attachment mechanism, such as a post with a barb, should be secure yet easy to use. Consider the visual impact of the earring from different angles, ensuring it complements the wearer's appearance.

sections.title: Technical Specifications
sections.content: Earrings should adhere to specific size and weight constraints to ensure comfort and safety. The post length should accommodate various ear thicknesses, and the barb should be designed to prevent accidental detachment. Materials used should be hypoallergenic to prevent skin irritation.

sections.title: Material and Attachment Methods
sections.content: Different headband designs utilize various materials and attachment methods. For instance, the BDB09 model uses a snap mechanism with PPco+PPco materials, while the BBD52 model employs glue with ABS+PVC90 materials. The BBD43 model also uses a snap mechanism but with PPco+PVC90 materials. The T7411 model uses a snap mechanism with PPco+PPco materials.

sections.title: Dimensional Specifications
sections.content: The headbands have specific dimensional requirements. One design features a width of 1.280 inches and a height of 1.200 inches, with an overall width of 1.455 inches. Another design has a width of 0.949 inches, a height of 1.199 inches, and an overall width of 1.102 inches.

sections.title: General Design Rules
sections.content: For necklaces with length greater than 1.5 inches, suggest an opening of 0.120 inches. The recommended material is PPCO. Ensure the shape matches the Torso's shape.

sections.title: Design Rule A
sections.content: If the length is between 0.9 and 1.5 inches, suggest an opening between 0.120 and 0.200 inches. The recommended material is PPCO. Ensure the shape matches the Torso's shape.

sections.title: Design Rule B
sections.content: If the length is between 0.1 and 0.5 inches, suggest an opening between 0.360 and 0.400 inches when the material is ABS (not too flexible). Ensure the shape matches the Torso's shape.

sections.title: Doll Necklace Design
sections.content: If the necklace is intended to fit a doll's neck with a length less than 0.5 inches, suggest an opening between 0.300 and 0.360 inches. The recommended material is PPCO and PVCO. Ensure the shape matches the Torso's shape.

sections.title: Space Optimization in Shoe Design
sections.content: Cut material inside the shoe to reserve more space for the foot, enhancing comfort and fit.

sections.title: Logo Placement on Shoe Soles
sections.content: For high heels, place the logo at the heel area. For platform shoes, position the logo centrally on the sole.

sections.title: Material Core Out in Toe-Cap
sections.content: Core out material from the toe-cap to avoid flow marks and shrinkage marks, improving the aesthetic and structural integrity of the shoe.

sections.title: Tampo Printing Effect
sections.content: Utilize tampo printing to achieve detailed designs on shoe surfaces, enhancing visual appeal.

sections.title: Wall Thickness Specifications
sections.content: The basic wall thickness for sunglasses should be 1.5 mm (0.059 inches). For the bridge, if the width is greater than 2 mm (0.079 inches), the wall thickness should remain at 1.5 mm (0.059 inches).

sections.title: Material Considerations
sections.content: Sunglasses can be made from C-PPCO raw resin, which provides a suitable balance of flexibility and durability.

sections.title: C-Clip Design Specifications
sections.content: The C-Clip is designed with specific dimensions to ensure proper functionality and compatibility with Chelsea hand accessories. The thickness of the clip is 1.5mm, providing adequate strength and durability. The internal diameter (ID) of the clip is 1.5mm, allowing it to securely hold onto the accessory. The opening of the clip measures 1.2mm, which facilitates easy attachment and detachment while maintaining a firm grip. The overall width of the clip is 1.4mm, ensuring a compact design that does not interfere with the accessory's usability.

sections.title: Horse Rein Standard Design
sections.content: The design of horse reins should consider ease of assembly and durability. Option B, which features one-piece molding and a hole with a slot, is preferred for easier assembly and enhanced strength.

sections.title: Seam Alignment
sections.content: Ensure proper alignment of seams during assembly to maintain aesthetic quality and structural integrity.

sections.title: Inner Runner Design
sections.content: The inner runner design should facilitate efficient material flow and support structural stability. Ensure the runner paths are optimized for the mold design.

sections.title: Hair Attachment
sections.content: Hair should be securely attached with appropriate width and tension to prevent detachment. Ensure the attachment points are robust and well-distributed.

sections.title: Head Design
sections.content: The horse head design should maintain a smooth contour with an angle not exceeding 40 degrees to ensure aesthetic appeal and structural integrity.

sections.title: Deco Peel Off
sections.content: Ensure that the decorative elements do not peel off. Check for proper adhesion and alignment during the manufacturing process.

sections.title: Surface Finish
sections.content: Avoid loss of matte finishing or welding issues due to thick wall design. Ensure consistent wall thickness to maintain surface quality.

sections.title: Projection Issue
sections.content: To avoid projection issues, ensure the tip of the horse's ears is forward above to less than 40 degrees.

sections.title: Gap Between Head and Hair
sections.content: Maintain a consistent gap between the head and hair to ensure proper fit and aesthetic appeal.

sections.title: Hair Attachment
sections.content: Secure the hair attachment with precise hole placement to ensure stability and durability.

sections.title: Dimensional Specifications
sections.content: Follow the specified dimensions for slots and hair placement to ensure proper assembly and appearance.

sections.title: Interference Fitting
sections.content: Use 3 tight lines as interference fitting to ensure stability and secure attachment of components.

sections.title: Loose Fitting
sections.content: Allow 0 to 0.005 inch/side for loose fitting to facilitate easy assembly and disassembly of parts.

sections.title: Doll Stand Components
sections.content: The doll stand consists of several components including the top, bottom, post, clip, dead weight, and friction pad. Each component plays a specific role in the assembly and stability of the stand.

sections.title: Gear Clearance Calculation
sections.content: The clearance between gears is calculated using the formula: \( D + C \), where \( D = \frac{m(Z1 + Z2)}{2} \). Here, \( m \) is the module, and \( Z1, Z2 \) are the number of teeth on the gears. The clearance values for different modules are specified as follows: 0.05mm for module 0.5, 0.06mm for modules 0.6 and 0.7, 0.06-0.07mm for module 0.8, 0.07mm for module 0.9, and 0.08mm for module 1.

For shoes, the cavity number should be placed at a visible location with dimensions of 2.3mm. For earrings, the cavity number should be placed with dimensions of 1.0-1.7mm.

sections.title: Gate Types for Gear
sections.content:
Different gate types have specific recommendations:

1. **Pin Point Gate (A)**: Not recommended due to too big runner ratio.
2. **Edge Gate (B)**: Recommended if structure allows for self-trimming.
3. **Sub Gate to Post in Cavity (C)**: Not recommended due to still needing trimming.
4. **Hot Runner with Many Drops (D)**: Not recommended due to high investment and use for high quota.
5. **New Design Edge Gate (E)**: Recommended as flange can increase gear strength, but gate needs trimming.

sections.title: Gear Clearance Calculation
sections.content:
Set the gear-center spacing to \(D+C\), where \(C\) is the clearance and:

\[
D=\frac{m(Z1+Z2)}{2}
\]

- \(m\) = module
- \(Z1\), \(Z2\) = numbers of teeth

sections.title: Overview of Hot Stamping

sections.title: Process Details

sections.title: Introduction to Snap Design
sections.content: Snap design involves creating interlocking components that can be easily assembled and disassembled. This is commonly used in plastic parts for toys, electronics, and other consumer products.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.content:
1. Ensure that dimension B is smaller than A for effective snap design. This allows for proper engagement and retention.
2. Overshoot or clearance is necessary for the snap to function effectively.
3. For cylindrical snaps, ensure that the diameter C is smaller than diameter D to maintain engagement.

sections.title: Structural Support
sections.content: When the snap is a separate small part, add a U-shaped rib to hold it. Additional support ribs may be needed to strengthen the structure.

sections.title: Sleeve Height Guideline
sections.content: When designing products, consider the risk of excessive plastic flow. Avoid using sleeves with an outer diameter (OD) less than 4mm and an inner diameter (ID) less than 2mm. Preferably, use sleeves with an ID greater than 3mm. Ensure the sleeve height meets the following requirements: 2 ≤ ID ≤ 5, L ≤ 4 * ID; ID > 5, L ≤ 6 * ID.

sections.title: Recommendation for Long Sleeves
sections.content: Due to the flow of adhesive, long sleeves may deform during assembly. Consider the direction of adhesive flow and minimize sleeve deformation by avoiding excessive adhesive application.

sections.title: Big Size Part Assembly
sections.content: For large parts, pre-assemble using 3-4 pins. Ensure a lead-in of 5mm to facilitate assembly.

sections.content: Ensure a minimum engagement of 5mm. Use a chamfer of 30° and a clearance of 0.75mm for proper fit. Maintain a radius of 0.20mm for stress relief.

sections.title: Male and Female Sleeve Specifications
sections.content: For male sleeves, use a 45° chamfer and maintain a diameter of ØB. For female sleeves, ensure a clearance of 0.75mm and a tolerance of B-0.10mm (0.25°/S).

sections.title: Introduction to Jetting and Flow Marks
sections.content: Jetting and flow marks are common defects in injection molding, often caused by improper flow of the molten material into the mold. These defects can affect the aesthetic and structural integrity of the final product.

sections.title: Causes of Jetting and Flow Marks
sections.content: Jetting occurs when the molten plastic enters the mold cavity at high speed, causing a snake-like pattern. Flow marks are usually caused by variations in the flow speed of the molten material, leading to visible lines on the surface.

sections.title: Improvement Techniques
sections.content:
1. **Adjust Injection Speed**: Reducing the injection speed can help in minimizing jetting by allowing the material to flow more smoothly into the mold.

2. **Optimize Mold Design**: Ensure that the mold design facilitates even flow of material. This includes proper placement of gates and runners.

3. **Temperature Control**: Maintain consistent temperature throughout the mold to prevent flow marks. Uneven cooling can lead to defects.

4. **Material Selection**: Use materials with appropriate viscosity to ensure smooth flow and reduce the likelihood of jetting and flow marks.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.content: By understanding the causes of jetting and flow marks and implementing the suggested improvements, manufacturers can enhance the quality of their injection molded products.

sections.title: Sealing Surface Improvement

sections.title: Structural Reinforcement

sections.title: Design Recommendations

2. **Accessibility**: Design for easy access to components for maintenance and assembly.
3. **Material Selection**: Choose materials that support the mechanical and thermal requirements of the components.
